thread:
sylvia: Quick heads-up — I pushed a small Helm change on feature/secret-hooks to register a K8s Secret via a Helm hook during chart install/upgrade. Trying to avoid a startup race where ExternalSecrets kicks in a bit later and our init container sees no secret.

sylvia: The idea is to create a placeholder secret with the right keys and an annotation that signals ExternalSecrets to take over (or skip reconcile briefly). Wanted a quick sanity check on RBAC + best practice before I open a PR.

tom: Can you paste the hook snippet? want to make sure we don't accidentally block upgrades.

sylvia: Sure — here's the core of the hook manifest I used:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: {{ template "fullname" . }}-db-credentials
  annotations:
    "helm.sh/hook": "post-install,post-upgrade"
    "helm.sh/hook-delete-policy": "hook-succeeded"
    "redwood.com/rotation-listener": "external-secrets"
type: Opaque
stringData:
  username: "placeholder"
  password: "placeholder"
```

sylvia: And for ExternalSecrets we have an ExternalSecret CR that claims the same name and will overwrite values once it syncs.

igor: Two quick things:
1) RBAC — the helm hook creating secrets needs the Tiller/helm service account perms in the cluster namespace (create/secrets). If you rely on the chart's install SA make sure it has that role. Example:

```yaml
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["secrets"]
  verbs: ["get", "create", "update", "delete"]
```

2) ExternalSecrets controller will see the secret name collision. By default it will try to reconcile and replace. Is that the desired flow? If the external secret is slow, apps might read placeholder values. Maybe add a readiness probe in the app or have the init container block until external-secret sets a specific annotation.

katie-bot: small recommendation — consider using `pre-install` hook with a `helm.sh/hook-weight` and `hook-delete-policy: before-hook-creation` if you want the placeholder removed before the controller notices; but that can be flaky on upgrades. Also `pre-upgrade` can cause issues with rollbacks.

sylvia: Good catch. My goal is: placeholder -> ExternalSecrets replaces -> apps start. I added an annotation `external-secrets.redwood.com/skip-reconcile: "true"` on the placeholder, then ExternalSecret controller will remove the flag after sync (managed by a short-lived controller job). But that's more complexity.

tom: Hmm I don't love special flags. Alternative: let ExternalSecrets create the secret, but have the Helm chart package include an ExternalSecret CR as part of the chart (so the resource exists and is reconciled). That avoids the collision and race.

igor: Yeah putting the ExternalSecret in the chart is cleaner. If you need a placeholder for DB migrations (pre-upgrade), do a job that waits on `ExternalSecretStatus` to be `Ready`.

sylvia: OK I'll open a PR that: (a) adds ExternalSecret CR to the chart, (b) adds RBAC note in values docs, (c) includes a simple `kubectl wait` smoke step for migrations. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/charts/pull/892 (draft)

tom: Ping @igor for review once it's ready. Also include an upgrade test in the smoke checklist.

igor: I'll take a look today. For smokecheck, verify these commands:

```bash
kubectl get externalsecret {{ .Release.Name }}-db-creds -n {{ .Release.Namespace }} -o yaml
kubectl get secret {{ .Release.Name }}-db-credentials -n {{ .Release.Namespace }} -o yaml
kubectl describe externalsecret/{{ .Release.Name }}-db-creds -n {{ .Release.Namespace }}
# check controller logs if it doesn't appear
kubectl logs -l app=external-secrets -n external-secrets | tail -n 200
```

sylvia: Thanks — I'll add those to the PR description and add a small pre-upgrade job template that can be enabled via values.

deploybot: deployment pipeline (chart-ci) triggered for sylvia/feature/secret-hooks — build 354 succeeded :white_check_mark:

tom: Awesome. @sylvia — when you mark PR ready, drop the checklist for me to approve for prod push (RBAC, smoke commands, rollout-rollback tested).

sylvia: Will do. One more note: if we ever switch to sealed-secrets for at-rest encryption we'd probably flip the chart to render a SealedSecret instead of a plain Secret — but that's future work.

katie-bot: FYI — added `security` label to the PR for audit.

sylvia: Thanks all — wrapping this up in the PR now.
